Avant-garde

/ah-vahnt-GARD/ - rhymes with guard · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Avant-garde means radically new and experimental, especially in art.

The choreographer's avant-garde piece unfolded in a parking garage, with dancers partnered by slow-moving forklifts.

Worked Example

For her thesis, the architecture student proposed a chapel of translucent concrete — no right angles, no fixed pews, walls that glowed at dusk. Half the jury refused to grade it; the other half kept it on display for a year. Both halves agreed the design was avant-garde: nothing in the program's hundred-year archive resembled it.

Avant-garde is more precise than 'new' or even 'experimental' because it means radically new and experimental, especially in art — the word is French for the advance guard, the soldiers sent ahead of the army. An avant-garde work is out in front of its whole field, past the point where any earlier model can guide it.

How Avant-garde Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

experimental

experimental: trying untried methods in any field, without leading a movement

cutting-edge

cutting-edge: at the newest stage of development, said mostly of technology

Antonyms

traditional

traditional: following forms handed down unchanged

mainstream

mainstream: what most people already watch, read, and buy

How Strong Is It? — fresh → experimental → avant-garde

fresh vs. avant-garde

fresh vs. avant-garde: Fresh praises a small newness — a fresh take on a sandwich — and stops far short of avant-garde.

experimental vs. avant-garde

experimental vs. avant-garde: Experimental goes further than fresh, actually testing untried methods, but it stops short of avant-garde, which breaks with every model that came before.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — avant

Root — avant: ahead, before (French)

Root — garde

Root — garde: guard (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Avant (ahead) + garde (guard) = the advance guard. In a marching army, the avant-garde went first, into ground no one had scouted. Nineteenth-century critics borrowed the term for artists working out ahead of the public's taste — and the military sense has since faded, leaving the artists holding the word.

Use the root in a new word: safeguard

Use the root in a new word: safeguard: A second set of brake cables safeguards the cable car if the first should ever snap.

Root Check

Word Choice

arts / critical

Avant-garde belongs to the arts and to writing about them: it says a work is radically new, out ahead of its whole field. For a new method in a lab or a classroom, experimental is the honest word; for something merely up to date, cutting-edge. In this unit, compare nascent, which says a thing has only just come into existence, whether or not it is daring.
